issues.title: Pass the gravy, hold the levy

takeaways.t: Stocks pared deep morning losses as the AI rout eased, with the Dow turning positive (+0.33%) while the Nasdaq slipped 0.62% and S&P 500 0.25%.
The 10-year yield fell 6 bps to 4.848%, extending its longest losing streak since 2024.
Crude rose 2.5% to $84.10 after the Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery.
October PCE inflation hit 3.8% year over year (3.6% prior) with core at 3.3%, keeping a December Fed hike in play.
The NRF sees holiday sales up 4.2% and Visa 4.5%, but Visa's inflation-adjusted growth is just 1.1%.
CrowdStrike's $44B Zscaler buy and Sanofi's $41B Insmed deal lifted 2026 global M&A to $4.7T, up 20% and a post-2021 high.

issues.title: Another one

takeaways.t: The US is reportedly set to announce new country-specific duties on China, the EU and 14 other nations, with overall rates capped at 15% for the EU, Japan and South Korea and up to 20% for China.
The Nasdaq fell 1.5% as the AI selloff resumed, and Anthropic closed 6.5% lower at $81.91, below its IPO price.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told employees he made terrible mistakes and is in therapy, while the stock kept sliding and probes continue.
Sanofi will buy Insmed for $41 billion, the industry's biggest deal in three years.
Roche's newly approved breast cancer pill could reach $14 billion in annual sales, priced at $22,500 per month in the US.
Dick's jumped over 14% after Foot Locker sales rose 0.5% in Q3 versus a feared 2% drop.

issues.note: Market numbers are the Tuesday close.

takeaways.t: Chipmakers pulled the Nasdaq down 1.48% and the S&P 500 down 0.50%, while the Dow rose 0.86% on rotation into cyclicals.
Consumer confidence hit a near two-year high; Best Buy comps rose 6.1% vs 2.3% expected, Kohl's jumped 19.78% and Abercrombie 19.87%.
Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $41B in cash, a 17% premium; Insmed rose 14.13% and Sanofi 10.97%.
Nvidia fell 5.86% despite Huang's return, Micron dropped 10.97% on a downgrade, and Analog Devices sank 17.37% on weak guidance.
Hyperscaler capex forecasts have stopped climbing, and they have issued over $250B of bonds this year, now 5.1% of investment-grade debt.
The 10-year slipped 1.0 bp to 4.904%, oil rose 1.58% to $81.44 and Bitcoin fell 2.65% to $59,642.
The Nasdaq jumped 6.51%, the S&P 500 gained 4.73% and the Dow rose 3.01%, rebounding from last week's selloff.
Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO 12 days after his ouster, and the stock surged 31.48%, adding nearly $1 trillion in market value.
Dell rose 20.76%, CoreWeave 22.32% and Bloom Energy 18.09%, while Arm gained 16.08% after its CEO extended his contract through 2033.
CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for $44B in stock, a 34% premium; Zscaler jumped 17.67% and CrowdStrike fell 8.95%.
The 10-year edged up 1.0 bp to 4.918% as bonds sold off, while oil fell 3.98% to $80.09 and Bitcoin added 0.63%.
Tesla gained 11.46% on a new self-driving release, Boeing rose 4.17% on a possible 250-plane China order, and International Paper fell 4.55%.

issues.title: Nvidia Drops 23%, AI Stocks Unwind, and Retail Defies the Selloff

takeaways.t: The S&P 500 lost 8.6%, its worst week since April 2025, and closed in correction with the Dow; the Nasdaq is now negative for 2026. Every sector ETF finished red, tech (XLK) -12.5% and staples best at -2.1%, and Friday's 3.7% drop was the seventh straight red day.
Nvidia beat and raised but sank 22.9% on the week after Reuters said the SEC is examining its accounting. Anthropic priced its IPO at $83, opened at $111.50 Thursday and faded to $88.91 by Friday.
Bonds rallied on growth fears: the 10-year fell 23 bp to 4.92% and the 2-year to 4.63%. A 25 bp hike on Dec 9 is still 90-97% priced, and Waller floated 50 bp to jolt inflation expectations.

Closed at 6,910, below the 200-day with RSI at 26, the lowest since April 2025. Resistance is 7,000, then Thursday's 7,175 close. Only 52.6% of S&P names sit above their 200-day, but VIX above 30 with RSI under 30 has Schwab looking for an oversold bounce.

At $424.39 after a 7.7% drop Thursday on a Hunterbrook short report about firmware reaching a blacklisted Chinese server maker. Bearish: a break below the daily 200SMA is her cue to join short 30-40 minutes after the open, targeting the $400s. Day trade; no position.

At $165.83 after Q3, with full-year sales growth guidance raised to about 6% and EPS to $10.65-11.40. Bullish since retail breakouts are holding: she wants pullbacks toward the 8EMA that hold the $163s. Swing idea; no position.

At $968.22. Tenji thesis: Trump's threat to penalize US firms building data centers abroad could hurt Equinix and Digital Realty's foreign builds and tenants, though the counter case is that AI demand kept at home could fill their US sites.
Flash PMIs Mon, consumer confidence Tue, then PCE, Q3 GDP, durable goods and the Beige Book Wed; markets closed Thu for Thanksgiving. Earnings: HPE, ZM Mon; DELL, BBY, WDAY, HPQ, ADSK Tue; DE Wed.

takeaways.t: The S&P 500 fell 3.70% into a correction, down over 10% from its peak, while the Nasdaq erased its 2026 gains and the Dow lost more than 1,000 points.
Shares fell 8.50% a day after the record $81.3B IPO, and Nvidia dropped 14.01% while Micron fell 13.89% and SK Hynix 13.11%.
Gold hit its lowest since September 2025 on bets for a December Fed hike, down over 30% from its January peak, with silver off about 64%.
The 10-year fell 14 bps to 4.912% as Treasurys rallied, and Bitcoin slid below $59,000, heading for its worst month in over four years.
AMD sank 13.25% after short-seller reports on China exports and up to $8.5B in guarantees backing its partners; the company says it follows export law.
Intuit fell 12.77% on a cut outlook and Sandisk 16.05%, while Gap rose 11.44% and Bill Holdings dropped 4.12% on a roughly $6B TPG and Corpay buyout.
All three indexes fell about 2%, with the Nasdaq headed for its longest losing streak since 2024.
Anthropic raised a record $81.3B, priced at $83 versus a $70-$78 range, valued near $1.5T, and shares jumped over 16%.
The 10-year held near 5.05% with a December hike possible, and gold lingered near a 14-month low.
Revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8B, e-commerce sales jumped 23% and the full-year sales forecast went up to 4.9%-5.2%.
PDD gained 11.04% and Palo Alto 6.42%, while AMD sank 7.72% and Williams-Sonoma dropped 15.16%.
Alphabet signed a 50 MW deal with Quaise for a roughly $350M Oregon volcano project to power data centers.

issues.title: Should you get in on Anthropic’s IPO?

takeaways.t: Nasdaq rose 0.42% but the Dow fell 1.11% and the S&P slipped 0.23%, even after Nvidia's strong earnings (shares -2.89%).
BofA's survey shows net tech overweight among fund managers dropped from 37% to 12%, the biggest monthly fall since 2006.
Trading may start tomorrow at a $1.5T-$1.6T valuation, after an offering aimed at up to $64.4B; Vanda sees about $250M of retail buying on day one.
15 of the 20 largest IPOs since 1990 fell below their offer price within a year, with a median drawdown of 40.9%.
Target raised guidance on 5.6% same-store sales growth and TJX beat on 4% comps; shares gained 3.97% and 8.12%.
UnitedHealth fell 10.21% on tougher fraud rules, Newmont dropped 6.05% as gold sank, and Take-Two rose 6.22% ahead of GTA VI.

issues.title: Home Depot hits a wall

takeaways.t: The Dow lost over 900 points (-1.64%) while the S&P fell 1.02% and Nasdaq 0.74%, with chipmakers leading ahead of Nvidia earnings.
Adjusted EPS of $3.86 beat by two cents and sales rose 4.9% to $43.4B, but a trimmed profit outlook sent shares down 2.55%.
The 30-year mortgage rate sits at 7.11%, existing-home sales fell 5.5% in October, and builder confidence hit a 14-year low.
Pricing is expected above the $70-$78 range at roughly a $1.4T valuation, raising about $64.4B, with trading set for Nov. 19 as ANT.
Jensen Huang resigned last week and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, with Nvidia reporting earnings Tuesday after the bell.
Salesforce sank 9.41%, Nike fell 6.35% after its investor day, and Deutsche Bank dropped 5.47%, while Sellas surged 156%.

issues.title: What's your beef?

takeaways.t: Nasdaq fell 2.49% and the S&P 1.91% ahead of Nvidia earnings after the bell Tuesday, while staples and healthcare rallied.
Shares slipped 4.12% as former CEO Jensen Huang's resignation kept fueling the selloff.
Bernstein pegs the hit to the four biggest airlines at $345M pretax after 18,500+ cancellations; L3Harris fell 3.92% on router scrutiny.
TELUS jumped 12.13% on a $21.96B Quebecor offer at a ~60% premium, and CG Oncology rose 13.95% on late-stage bladder cancer data.
Shares rose 8%+ on an earnings beat, though it guides revenue down 3.5%-5.5% and beef prices are up 8.7% this year.
Bitcoin hovered near $65,000, and Strategy sank 7.70% as the price fell below its ~$75,452 average cost.

issues.title: The Market Bounced. Nvidia Could Decide What Happens Next.

takeaways.t: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq snapped four-week losing streaks; Nasdaq had its best week since August. All 11 sectors rose, led by energy (XLE +5.4%), but Friday money rotated out of tech into staples.
Jensen Huang resigned Thursday and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. The stock fell a sixth straight week (about -12%) and closed under $4T market cap. Earnings Tue Nov 17.
October CPI ran hot (headline +0.4%, core +0.3%). The 10-year jumped 29 bp to 5.152% and the 2-year 35 bp to 4.872%. A December hike is now fully priced; Waller says 50 bp deserves a look.
7,600 flipped to resistance, with the 7,620 June high just above. Schwab calls it bearish until 7,600 is reclaimed. Nasdaq sits on its 200-day; Russell and SOX are below theirs.
At $36.65 after its 21st straight beat-and-raise (revenue +46%). Testing all-time highs near $38. Leaning bullish: a reclaim and hold above $38 sets up a trend-join long. Swing idea.
At $188.12. Reclaimed the daily 200SMA and is consolidating above $180-185; a break of the consolidation and downtrend could start a reversal. She is long from about $188.60 as a swing.

At $162.85. The DOJ reportedly opened a probe the day Huang resigned; AMD is flagged as the other side of the trade. Bull case: demand (guided about $108B) could outlast the scandal. Needs a chart setup first.
Data: Warsh speaks Mon, retail sales Tue, FOMC minutes Wed, Philly Fed Thu. Anthropic prices its IPO Wed and trades Thu. Earnings: HD, DIS, NVDA Tue; LOW, TJX, PANW Wed; GAP, ROST Thu.

issues.title: Inflation gobbles the savings

takeaways.t: October PPI rose 0.3% on the month and 6.5% on the year, the biggest annual jump in nearly four years, though below forecasts.
Markets price an 89% chance of a quarter-point hike on Dec 8-9, with an 11% chance of a half-point move.
Nvidia slipped 2.01% for a sixth straight weekly loss, and Bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time since August, triggering about $1.3B in liquidations.
Cerebras jumped 11.22% on earnings and a Microsoft deal, Modine surged 27.84% on Samsung takeover talk, and Cisco fell 6.24% despite a beat.
A 12-hour Microsoft 365 outage could cost $300M-$500M in insured losses, though the stock was flat.
Sales rose 13% and half-year profit 39%, but shares fell over 4% as jewelry growth slowed to 14% versus 16% expected.

issues.title: AI Stocks Drop Hard, But These Setups Are Getting Interesting

takeaways.t: Thursday did the damage: semis fell about 12% and the Nasdaq about 5.5% in one session on fears that data center limits after the midterms slow AI spending. The VIX touched 28, its highest since March.
October payrolls came in at 165,000 vs 65,000 expected and unemployment fell to 4.1%. December hike odds rose to about 78%; the 10-year closed at 4.86%.
Broke the 7,600 double-top neckline, which is now resistance. Next target is the 200-day near 7,300. Nasdaq-100 is under its 200-day with RSI below 30.
Breadth is stretched (70%+ of S&P stocks above the 50-day, McClellan above +100) and large speculators are near the 97th percentile net long Nasdaq futures.
At $387.38 after a 20% earnings gap that held through the tech selloff. Cautiously bullish: wants a reclaim of $380-390, a break of the daily downtrend and a reclaim of the 200SMA. Swing idea.
At $186.64 after the AI unwind. Waiting for a clear green market day and buying strength after 10:30-11 AM around $190-195 rather than catching the knife. Day-trade idea; same plan for AMD, SNDK.
At $303.35. Strong hiring plus high yields help payroll firms (ADP, PAYX) through more workers and interest on client funds. Bear case: slower hiring or falling yields. Needs a chart setup first.
Data: CPI Tue, jobless claims Thu, PPI Fri; bond market closed Wed. Earnings: TTWO, RKLB, HIMS, OXY Mon; ONON, CRWV Tue; CSCO, AMAT, NBIS Thu.

issues.title: AI Stocks Crack While Retail and Energy Take the Lead

takeaways.t: A Friday chip rout made it a third straight weekly loss for the S&P 500, while the Russell 2000 was the only major index up on the week (+1.3%).
Intel fell 28.6% and the semiconductor index dropped 7.2% Friday; Amazon (-$42.4B trailing FCF), Alphabet and Meta are all burning cash on AI capex.
The Fed held at 3.75% to 4.00% with two dissents for a hike (December hike near 76%), and WTI sits at $104.12 after a 15% October gain.
Support at 7,500 then the 200-day near 7,300; resistance at 7,800. The 7,600 to 7,680 band held eight times since June.
Leaning bullish at $150.52 after a gap to 52-week highs on strong earnings. Watching the $148-150 area to join the trend; the thesis fails below $140. Better as a swing than intraday.
At $154.03 after new all-time highs on analyst upgrades. Would consider a pullback toward the 8EMA near $146-149 with risk under $145. Earnings Nov 5, and a big gap down would void the setup.
Data: ISM Mon, JOLTS Tue, ADP Wed, jobs report Fri. Earnings: AAPL and PLTR Mon; AMD, AMGN, ANET, SHOP Tue; DASH, UBER, APP, COHR Wed; ABNB, LITE, AAOI Thu.
